key_insight: A high-order multiscale method captures heterogeneous, fractionally damped wave propagation with a proven O(ε) global energy-norm error bound.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a lower-cost alternative to fully resolved simulations of wave propagation in composites with strong material contrasts and history-dependent attenuation.
method: Derive a homogenized wave equation with first- and second-order multiscale corrections.
Combine finite elements and finite differences using an L2-1σ–Newmark time scheme.
Establish local residual cancellation, global error bounds, and unconditional shifted-energy stability.
evidence_signal: Two- and three-dimensional numerical examples demonstrate accuracy, efficiency, reduced computational cost, and robustness; the abstract provides no numerical speedup figures.
watch_item: Fractional history dependence remains an implementation concern; the abstract does not quantify long-time memory or storage costs.
paper_title: A high-order multi-scale method and its error analysis for nonlocal-in-time fractionally damped wave problems in composite materials
